Demonstrates the three infrastructure pieces: generated impl (infrastructure.connectors), handwritten helper machinery seam (infrastructure.process outer domain), assembly (infrastructure.bootstrap).

origins.description: This input explicitly defines the implementation shape, MANUAL marker grammar, helper injection contract and delegation guarantees. Not historical truth, not approved production business semantics.

legalDomain.manualMarkers: Exact four-space comment lines '// ==== BEGIN MANUAL ====' and '// ==== END MANUAL ===='; exactly one pair per override method; BEGIN sits on the line after the def opening brace, the delegation body on the single following line, END followed by the method closing brace. Pairing is pinned as a structural property with a directed negative.
legalDomain.delegationContract: Exactly one runner call per port call; the script argument or the bound script constant is passed to the runner verbatim — never escaped, rewritten, defaulted or trimmed; the raw output line is lifted through the companion decode into the typed result; no retry, no exception swallowing, no synthesized success, no timeout or recovery logic in the generated class.
legalDomain.failureChannels: A failed runner Future propagates unchanged as the port call's failed Future; a runner failure thrown synchronously propagates out of the port call itself unchanged (same exception instance, exactly one invocation recorded); a malformed runner output becomes a named ProtocolViolation on the failure channel through the codec; a refusal stays a typed value on the success channel.
legalDomain.helperInjection: The single handwritten helper NodeSubprocessRunner is a constructor parameter of the generated class under @Inject(); helpers live in the infrastructure.process handwritten outer domain and are never created by the generator; parameterless port methods use the bound script constant "stockreservation/location-directory.v1" verbatim.
legalDomain.runner: NodeSubprocessRunner.run performs exactly one subprocess execution per call and yields one output line; concrete spawn/timeout/exit-code mechanics are handwritten in infrastructure.process and are outside the quality gate's executable surface (the sandbox denies process-exec); the gate verifies compile, seam contract via scripted and throwing doubles, and delegation behavior — never a live process.
legalDomain.assembly: infrastructure.bootstrap.StockCatalogModule binds the port to the implementation with an explicit Guice binding; the kernel-facing application layer carries no implementation reference; the test seam module supplies runner and ExecutionContext instances so the assembly property resolves the real binding.
legalDomain.unusedSlot: The raw no-helper branch (defaultBody '???') is a synchronous unimplemented slot, not a constructed failed Future; its generated shape is deferred to generator-phase fixtures and is not claimed by this sample.

decisions.choice: CANDIDATE RULING for walkthrough ratification: the implementation mirrors the FULL approved port ABI — both methods, both parameter shapes — fixing the raw Builder's first-method-only/parameters-Nil defect (diff 5.1) that is type-incompatible with the approved port; the no-helper '???' and multi-helper profiles are documented as raw shapes and deferred to generator-phase fixtures, never faked into this sample.

Runner ABI is run(script: String): Future[String] as the single overload; parameterless methods pass the bound script constant verbatim; the script argument is never escaped or rewritten; concrete subprocess mechanics (spawn, timeouts, exit codes) are handwritten in infrastructure.process and explicitly NOT executed inside the quality gate — gate coverage is compile plus seam-contract doubles (scripted success/failure queue and synchronous thrower), never a live process (diff 11.3).

USER RULING 2026-11-18 carried over: no @ImplementedBy — the multi-module (隔离区) kernel form has no implementation classes in the kernel module. The impl name is connectorName + 'Impl' and assembly is the explicit infrastructure.bootstrap.StockCatalogModule Guice binding, byte-identical with the approved port bundle.

Multi-module isolation form: generated impl in infrastructure.connectors, handwritten helper source in infrastructure.process (手写外域, BC PackageLayout L105-L111 — the generator never creates that file), assembly in infrastructure.bootstrap; the direction-aware boundary import gate enforces kernel isolation. Recorded divergence: the approved port bundle kept its runner seam inside infrastructure.connectors as a port-sample support file; this family moves the helper to infrastructure.process per this family's own contract — the port bundle stays frozen as approved.

MANUAL block ownership: the marker grammar and pairing are frozen as a structural property with a directed negative; the block content is the delegation body and regeneration byte-preservation is a writer contract verified at the generator phase, not claimed by this Scala sample; a helper's synchronous failure and a failed runner Future both propagate unchanged, never converted.

Deferred to owners: connector-assembly-integrator owns the product registration and iface+impl plan; shared writers own mergeManual/ledger/anchors; the single noteId/method-anchor mapping (D5) stays out of this sample — no @knowledge comment is fabricated here.
